sections.title: Report description and field lists
sections.what: Describes what the report covers, reads the industry option, and defines which stored field names count as planned or actual cost, planned or actual completion date, and delay.
sections.why: The field lists must match what the scan reads, so the audit counts the same inputs the scan would use.
sections.watch_out: If the Reality Scan changes the field names it reads, these lists must change too or the counts will drift.

sections.name: main
sections.title: Per-industry coverage report
sections.what: For each industry, counts projects, evidence, facts, findings and company links. Checks which projects have cited cost and schedule inputs. Resolves the scan scope and loads the Lessons Learnt factbase and Opportunity Map feed. Prints the latest runs and a JSON summary.
sections.why: Shows how much data each tool can see before anyone runs it.
sections.watch_out: It loads every industry and the whole project feed in one pass, so large data makes it slow.

summary: Read-only report showing, for each industry, what data each analysis tool can see.
purpose: Shows how many projects, facts, findings and links exist per industry, and how many projects have the cost and schedule inputs the Reality Scan tool needs.
why: The header describes it as the ceiling before a live source re-check. Likely reason: to check tool readiness before running tools on an industry.
how: Lists the industries that have projects and, for each one, counts Yard records and checks which projects have cited cost and schedule inputs. Resolves the scope the Reality Scan would use, loads the Lessons Learnt factbase, counts the Opportunity Map profiles and news, and lists the latest runs for the industry. Prints everything as JSON.
inputs: The projects, evidence_quotes, compass_findings, company_project_links, reality_scan_runs and lessons_learnt_runs tables, the project feed, and the industry list.
outputs: A JSON report printed to the console.
risks: Loads every industry and the whole project feed at once, so it is slow on large data. The header says it writes only the research-source registration that Lessons Learnt runs make, but this file does not show that registration.
debug: Pass the industry option to check one industry. If an industry shows zero inputs, check its project URLs and field names against the lists at the top of the file.
